Изометрическая пошаговая рпг, продажи которой закрыли, видимо из-за особой её популярности. 
Разрабы решили усложнить игроку жизнь, заставив играть только с смартфона, безальтернативно, вычеркнув клавиатуру и мышь (которой нужно щёлкать в главном меню по настройками и нажимать play, что бы игру собственно начать) из геймплея. Как вы понимаете это не для удобства сделано, играть на телефоне максимально противно и неудобно, он проигрывает "традиционным контроллерам" в пух и прах. Все диалоги и действия в бою выводятся на его экран и игроку постоянно приходится на него переводить взор с экрана монитора - туда-обратно, всегда. Удобно ли это и помогает погружению в игру?! Нет конечно! Телефон не обладает тактильной отдачей, это плоский кирпич, по экрану которого водишь большим пальцем держа в ладони руки, что бы персонаж на мониторе перемещался - это единственный момент когда ты смотришь на монитор не отрывая от него глаза и так ещё можно играть, но когда нужно делать какие-то действия, или любой диалог или разговор с неписем, или ты вступил в бой где иконки всех видов атак тоже выводятся на экран телефона, вот тут начинается "бегание туда-сюда глазами", потому что, что бы что-то сделать тебе необходимо перевести взгляд на телефон, без этого ты ничего не сможешь сделать "на ощупь" пальцами . И как вы думаете интересно ли играть в такой геймплей?! Конечно нет. Разрабы решили воплотить в жизнь изврат в управлении, но естественно ничего путного из этого не получилось.
Больше всего удивляют исключительно положительные отзывы на игру, как будто они все проплаченные (не утверждаю), чего быть в принципе не должно. И судя по достижениям, где прелюдию осилило всего лишь 25%, хвалильщиков на долго играть не хватило.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Just finished this game with my family. It was nice to have a good couch co-op CRPG to spend quality time with friends and family in-person. Besides Secret of Mana, there really aren't a lot of them that are rich with story and character progression. And this definitely had both.

What I liked:
- Separate apps allow you to review your quests, loadouts, skills, and stats while you're following someone or just pausing your exploration as a group.
- The skill trees had choices that mattered. Weapon and ability stances (causing stat shifts after switching to different class abilities) really made you think about which trees to push harder even if the only new things from certain points on were "just" increased bonuses.
- Combat flowed well. It is turn based and there is strategy to choosing the order in which heroes take their turns between enemy turns.
- Taking turns reading text can be fun. It can also be annoying sometimes, but the interaction of the group is higher and I generally liked it.
- The story was engaging and the characters interesting. They had some good interactions (We had the crusader/witch hunter and the witch trying to work together).
- The voice acting was good. 
- There are secret dialog and missions that you don't have to tell anyone else about.

What I didn't like:
- The phone-based virtual control is clunky (like ported console games that require a d-pad control on your touchscreen phone).
- They ended after season 1!!!  I came in late and I'm really sad that they didn't have the funding to make the rest of it work.

Even without a complete story, it was an experience I am glad I had the pleasure of having.

Really fun game with a couple of friends. No other experience like it.

But there are some things I really wish they'd change:

- The game has 6 different currencies that are used in various combinations. It's as horribly confusing as a pay to win mobile game. E.g. You spend some currency to make a healing potion, only to find you can't level up an ability because it uses the same currency.
- Each player competes to find currencies, making the game anti-cooperative. During battles players position themselves near loot to grab it first in a race, to the detriment of the team fight. Mages are left at the back to be poor.
- The UI is poorly explained and unintuitive. E.g. my paladin had a sword strike skill that disappeared after a few minutes, perhaps when I learnt a new skill. He can't talk to other players, but they can talk to him, no explanation of how the big wheel of actions is supposed to work. There are no tooltips on any attributes to explain what they do. The abilities/upgrades are all mixed together in various ways and hard to understand.
- The UI is designed for right handed phone users, with no setting to switch sides. My left thumb kept bumping the bottom left button and triggering inadvertent potion use. Annoying.
- There is no minimap and the camera is zoomed in closely, so it's sometimes difficult to figure out where to go to find the final room in a quest in a huge castle.

This game will frustrate you. 

It's a blast to play this with friends in a couch co-op environment.  I played with a pair of buddies for about 5 hours one evening, and it was great fun.  I'm not sure how close we came to finishing all the content.  Maybe we only made it through episode 1.  It was a fun experience.  Our biggest issue was charging our smartphones that weren't fully charged when we sat down.

Everyone being able to control their characters using their own phone was clever, though not an improvement over, say, just having their own controller.  The great part of this was when the game revealed secrets to us via our smart phone, and gave us dialogue that we could voice act as we wished.  It's was embarrassing and fun.  

But, as you might have read, the game ceased further updates when the money dried up, which means the story just stops.  This is the frustrating bit, and the primary reason why someone might leave a bad review. 

However, this game needs to be experienced, if only for the novelty of it.  There are some visionary RPG elements at work here utilizing technology that the majority of gamers are going to have on them.  Another game in this same vein needs to be made in the future or, barring that, a new tabletop RPG that seamlessly integrates this type of technology.  Or, best yet, some blend of the two, where publishers develop game content that is then run on a tabletop, with various checks and rolls being handled by a program, and world-building information fed to the characters to relay to their fellows IN CHARACTER, as they deem fit.  There is so much potential here, and every RPG fan needs to play Eon Altar if only to see for themselves what the future could hold.

TL;DR - if you're into tabletop role-playing games, this is definitely a must-buy then play with your group.

Klassischer Fall von Daumen zur Seite. Interessantes Spielprinzip welches öfter existieren sollte jedoch mit starken Kritikpunkten. Leider wird dieses Spiel nicht mehr aktualisiert, weshalb eine Änderung diesbezüglich nicht mehr umgesetzt wird. Perfektes Couch Coop Spiel mit ein bisschen Tiefgang und leichten RPG Elementen. Perfekt um es auf einen großen Bildschirm oder Fernseher (eines von beiden ist Unbeding zu Empfehen!) zu Streamen.


----Optik:
Sehr dunkles Spiel. Grafik Niveau am PC liegt in der Ecke von älteren RTS wie Warcraft 3. Nett Gezeichnete Lade und Hintergrundbilder. Grafik am Handy umfasst einen schön gezeichneten Hintergrund und simplen Grafiken für die Items und Fähigkeiten. Ansonsten auch sehr leicht gehalten und keine übertriebene Augenweide. Animationen in Cut Scenes sollte man auch nicht synchron mit der Tonspur erwarten. Es läuft alles flüssig, insbesondere die Angriffsanimationen.

---Sound:
Netter Hintergrundsound und Musik. Kann sich mal geben. Gegner und NPCs auf Englisch vollvertont. Für die persönliche Note sind [spoiler] die eigenen Charaktere selbst zu sprechen. [/spoiler]

--- Gameplay:
Das Spiel ist ein angehauchtes RTS mit PnP Elementen. Gespielt wird es vor einem Bildschirm mit einem Gerät wie Smartphone oder Tablett. Funktioniert mit bisher jedem von mir getestetem Gerät einwandfrei. Die App gibt es in den entsprechenden Stores. Hier gibt es die meisten Kritikpunkte. Um sich mit dem Spiel zu verbinden muss das Gerät über WLAN verbunden werden. Das Netzwerk muss zwingend hierbei das selbe sein wie der PC an dem das Spiel läuft. Eine Spielsuche über das Internet oder eine Verbindung wie z.B. über Bluethoot gibt es leider nicht. Die Verbindung wird einem nirgendwo angezeigt. Heißt wenn diese nicht stark ist, bemerkt man dies nicht. Das Handling am Smartphone ist einfach. Man hat eine Schaltfläche mit welcher man seinen Charakter bewegt. Alle gesprochenen Texte werden auf dem Smartphone angezeigt. Entscheidungen werden gemeinsam mittels geheimer Wahl getroffen oder betreffen nur einzelne Charaktere. Cool ist hierbei das jeder die Möglichkeit bekommt Geheimnisse zu bewahren oder diese auszusprechen. Das Menü selbst mit dem Charakter ist darauf ausgelegt ein Tablett zu nutzen, am Smartphone geraten manche Schaltflächen sehr winzig. Ebenfalls genial sind so Möglichkeiten Charaktere miteinander zu koppeln. So muss sich nur ein Spieler um das Bewegen kümmern und die Anderen folgen automatisch. Handel geht auch leicht über das Smartphone. 
Das Laufen und Erkunden ist in Echtzeit. Die Kämpfe sind Rundenbasiert. So kommt keine Hektik auf und der Kampf kann geplant werden. Eventuelle Ungenauigkeiten durch die Steuerung werden hier durch das durchklicken durch die Gegner ausgehebelt.
Als letzten großen Kritikpunkt: Die Kamera! Eine Ausgeburt der Hölle. Man dachte sowas wäre nicht mehr existent, jedoch EON hat es geschafft diese wiederzubeleben. Die Kamera ist mehr oder minder statisch mit keiner Möglichkeit der Einflussnahme. So klemmt man dann an Hindernissen fest weil man die Kamera nicht drehen kann und die Steuerung leicht unpräzise ist oder findet simple Wege nicht, weil eine Mauer in der Sicht ist...
Das Spiel lässt sich an Speicherpunkten speichern. Das Laden von Spielständen benötigt etwas Hirnschmalz. Da man sich selbst merken muss wie viele Spieler und wer mit welchem Charakter gespielt hat. Fremde Charaktere oder zu viele Spieler werden mit Level 1 mit hinein geworfen.


--- Inhalt: 
Story ist generisch. Gut und Böse und man selbst als Angeheuertes Etwas mit Geheimnissen das Versucht allem auf die Schliche zu kommen. Die Story wird leider nicht zu ende geführt das die Entwickler es nie zu ende geschrieben haben.



--- Community und Entwickler:

Eon Altar is a small, but fun, couch co-op fantasy role-playing game meant to be enjoyed with friends. 

[b]Technical Info:[/b] The use of mobile devices with a free app as a controlled makes couch co-op relatively simple, although [i]I recommend charging before and after playing[/i]. The game itself is hosted over the local Wi-fi network. 

[b]The Story[/b] is actually incomplete. From what I've read in old steam community discussions, the developers intended several episodes to be made. Unfortunately, the game did not sell well and so development stopped years ago. Episode 3 unfortunately ends on something of a cliffhanger as a result, buuut there's a good boss battle, and it's an alright ending given how abrupt it could otherwise have been. 

[b]Personal Questlines and objectives[/b] come with each of the five playable characters. Sometimes they're basic tasks that relate to the character. Examples: leading the party as the healer-paladin, or looting as the greedy sellsword. Playing with a group of friends and co-ordinating with one another to complete everyone's personal quests was fun for me personally. Player characters can also have conversations with each other, and relationship meters (seen on the Stats menu) can actually change depending on the things players choose for their character to say. I'm afraid I largely played this game solo, but in a few sessions with friends this interesting interaction came up. D&D players (like myself) might enjoy it, especially given all player character dialogue is not voiced, but meant to be spoken aloud by the players. 

[b]The Main Story[/b], on the other hand, is only kind of alright. Right at the start of the game, there are lots of phantasy names that will probably go over a new player's head. Obviously the main story involves the titular Eon Altar, but from a gameplay perspective it feels like the main story is held together by somewhat bland objectives. Sometimes trying to find an objective requires walking around a maze of tunnels blindly, and the camera is irritating about 10% of the time. 

That said, the *combat gameplay* is a finished product, and is this game's prime attraction I think. Each of the five characters plays a very unique role in combat: a healer that can swing a sword, a mage that casts fireball, a barbarian that fights at low health, and a tank that draws aggression. Combine these unique roles with friendly fire on many abilities, and suddenly playing battles with your friends becomes very engaging. 

Just now, before I wrote this review, I finished the game's story a second time over and was quite fatigued. Rather than do it more for some story achievements, I decided to dip my toes into the game's 
[b]Combat Arena:[/b] Where story is non-existent and players can fully enjoy combat after combat of increasingly difficult enemies. Unlike in the story where players begin with nothing, in the Combat Arena everyone is given a large number of resources to upgrade their abilities and craft items for the coming fight. I highly recommend players complete Episode 1's prelude before jumping into the Arena, just so they understand what upgrades do and how the combat works at a basic level. Personally, it was a lot of condensed fun compared to the campaign. 

Finally, [b]there is one guide[/b] out there for this game, but it's a good one. Hosted on GameFAQs, it's got the basics, some text-crafted maps, walkthroughs, achievement descriptions, and explanations of some in-game mechanics. I'd recommend giving it the quick Ctrl+F if you have questions while playing the game. That or Google. 

[b]TL;DR[/b]
Eon Altar is a fun couch co-op fantasy role-playing game. The best way to enjoy it is with friends coming over for a visit. Give the prelude a whirl, then sink your teeth into the Episode 1 Combat Arena together. I got to Wave 15 solo on Normal difficulty, so aim for that. I also think D&D groups might enjoy this game if they meet regularly. 
~Fin

I'm at the beginning of the third episode rn, so I haven't had a complete playthrough and reserve my right to change opinion later, but so far, I recommend this game if you have friends to play for a longer period of time. The game has a cool backstory and each character has its own backstory and interests, so its better if you can play it consistently without great time lapses, just like a pen and paper RPG.

It's fun to have this tension between cooperation and competition and this slow sensation of building trust and relationships, just like a pen and paper RPG, but without the necessity of having a DM available to creat/run the campaign.

The concept of having the phone as a controller is really nice and although its a bit clumsy at the beggining it gets better once you get the hang of it. I really hope more games buy into this idea.

There are still some minor bugs and annoyances, like the inability to have independent control of movement/positioning and attack, or how sometimes the camera can be stuck at some point and not really show what you're trying to see in the room, but those are, in my opinion, small issues compared to the big picture.

Even in the hardest difficulty the game can be a bit easy,, once you start acting as a coordinated party, but that doesn't take the fun out of it, since it's rewarding a good strategy. 

I look forward to seeing more episodes in the future, sequels or different characters to play with, even though I know the requirements of the game (at least two people to sit through the entire campaign) it's a major constrain to its player base size and by extent, its profitability.

+ Very fun game to play with family and friends.
+ The fact that you can play this game with your phone is extremely practical. No need to bring extra gear, or have a specific place to play it. Just start it up and use the phone with a home wifi. Everyone has a phone and a home wifi these days.
+ The way dialogue is implemented is fun. In general you can see the dialogue that the game offers you, but if a player character says something the player actually has to say it because the rest can't see. It's a bit dorky but it adds a roleplaying layer that you can use for immersion or comedy.
+ Every class adds something unique to the game in tactics. The skills and abilities are quite simple for people who are familiar with RPG's, but a bit challenging for the newbs. This challenge is easily overcome by guiding or just throwing it out there in a trial and error sense. (have had multiple occasions where my sister used an AoE and fireblasted my ass). All this adds to comedy in my opinion.
+ Turn based combat system without any pressure of time helps tremendously and just makes a very relaxing and engaging experience where all players try to come up with tactics to tackle a battle.
+ Every character has dynamics between each other. You can improve the relationships between the characters or let it rot. You do this by engaging in a dialogue with another player. 
+- ^This can take some time if all 4 players want to see the dynamics between each other.
+- You need to get used to the movement controls, but you will get there in 5 minutes so don't worry about it too much; Movement precision is far from important.
+- This game is a multi-session endeavor. If you are searching for something to play in one evening maybe you can play one episode, but to play the full three episodes (which i recommend) you need to have multiple sessions.
- Be careful with objectives and goals. Sometimes if a certain action gets interrupted while in dialogue of a quest step by let's say combat, you can't trigger the step again so you can continue. This happens only rarely though.

All in all a great game for people to get into RPG's. The turnbased system makes the game very casual, and I love playing this with my friends, family and girlfriend. The last 2 are not that into gaming in general at all, and they like it a lot. Be sure to pick it up.
